item.text: {"search_note":"I found no 2024 evidence that Modi personally launched a new nuclear arms-control, inspection, or disarmament treaty initiative. The record is mostly continuation of India’s longstanding doctrine and support for multilateral disarmament language, not a new Modi-specific breakthrough. So the best reading is: qualified support overall, but with visible limits and at least one clear anti-arms-control vote.","evidence":[{"title":"Priorities for the 78th Session of the United Nations General Assembly","publisher":"Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India","date":"2024","url":"https://www.mea.gov.in/india-priorities-unga","summary":"India states it is “steadfast” in universal, non-discriminatory, verifiable nuclear disarmament, accepts a doctrine of credible minimum deterrence and no-first-use, and supports immediate negotiations on an FMCT in the Conference on Disarmament. This is the clearest official evidence that Modi’s government backed disarmament and arms-control processes in principle.","question_ids":["1B.4"]},{"title":"Increasing Confrontation Involving States with Nuclear-Weapon Capabilities ‘Most Dangerous’ International Security Threat, First Committee Told","publisher":"UN Meetings Coverage / Press Releases","date":"1 Nov 2024","url":"https://press.un.org/en/2024/gadis3754.doc.htm","summary":"The UN report says India’s speaker reaffirmed an “undiminished commitment” to universal, non-discriminatory, verifiable nuclear disarmament and a step-by-step multilateral framework, while also restating credible minimum deterrence and no-first-use. This supports a good-faith reading of India’s 2024 disarmament posture.","question_ids":["1B.4"]},{"title":"The Wilmington Declaration Joint Statement from the Leaders of Australia, India, Japan, and the United States","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office / PIB","date":"22 Sep 2024","url":"https://www.pib.gov.in/pressreleasepage.aspx?PRID=2057454&lang=2&reg=48","summary":"As a joint statement signed by Modi, the Quad reaffirmed peace and stability, opposed destabilizing actions by force or coercion, and endorsed peaceful resolution of disputes. This is de-escalatory evidence, though it is not a nuclear-arms-control agreement.","question_ids":["1B.4","1B.1"]},{"title":"English Translation of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's remarks at the United Nations 'Summit of the Future'","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office / PIB","date":"23 Sep 2024","url":"https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2058077&lang=2&reg=48","summary":"Modi said “Success of Humanity lies in our collective strength, not in the battlefield.” That is broad anti-escalatory rhetoric and supports the de-escalation side of 1B.4, but it is not itself a treaty or inspection commitment.","question_ids":["1B.4","1B.1","1B.2"]},{"title":"In 79 Separate Recorded Votes, First Committee Approves 24 Drafts on Nuclear Weapons, Including Traditional Text on Road Map to Nuclear-Weapon-Free World","publisher":"UN Meetings Coverage / Press Releases","date":"1 Nov 2024","url":"https://press.un.org/en/2024/gadis3754.doc.htm","summary":"The report says the CTBT draft passed with 177 in favour, 0 against, and 5 abstentions, including **India**. Abstention is not outright opposition, but it is evidence that India did **not** fully endorse this key nuclear-test-ban text in 2024.","question_ids":["1B.4"]},{"title":"First Committee Sends 14 Drafts to General Assembly on Regional Disarmament, UN Disarmament Machinery, Deferring Action until Tomorrow on Three Key Texts","publisher":"UN Meetings Coverage / Press Releases","date":"7 Nov 2024","url":"https://press.un.org/en/2024/gadis3758.doc.htm","summary":"The report says a draft on conventional arms control at regional and subregional levels passed 179-1, with **India voting against**. That is direct counterevidence to broad support for arms-control agreements in 2024.","question_ids":["1B.4"]}]}
